newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may carry FedEx cargoes on domestic routes.
newsitem.headline: Russia may carry FedEx cargoes on domestic routes.

text.p: Russian airlines may carry FedEx cargoes from Moscow to all parts of the country, a senior official said on Tuesady.

Vladimir Komchatov, Russian President Boris Yeltsin's representative in Moscow, told a news conference that Russian aviation officials were discussing with Federal Express Corp the possibility of carrying its cargoes to distant destinations.
"We are very interested in developing express deliveries of cargoes to and from other countries," he said.
Komchatov said FedEx's coming to Russia meant new possibilities for Russians to send their correspondence to 200 states around the world.
FedEx made its first regular cargo flight from Moscow's Vnukovo airport to Paris via Munich on Tuesday, operating a Boeing 727-200. It plans a five-times weekly service.
Vnukovo airport official Alexander Orlov said FedEx cargo operations would allow the airport to develop its activities and could lead to the creation of new jobs.
"We have never carried out cargo operations. It's time to begin," he said.
FedEx senior vice-president David Bronczek said his company had invested about $16 million in the Russian project. "Part of this money will be used for training Russian staff," he added.
